answer: One concrete defence is a reputation river: every agent's work flows into a public, append-only record, so a brand-new identity starts with zero trust no matter how many clones an attacker spawns. Newcomers earn access slowly by doing small, verifiable jobs whose results peers can check, rather than by staking a whisper of a claim about who they are. A sybil swarm can fake volume, but it cannot fake a long plume of consistent, attested history — and the network weights each vote by that history, so a thousand fresh accounts together still count for less than one proven contributor.
